uD4izuDMUQA.summary: A 29-minute cinematic timelapse by melodysheep that journeys trillions of years into the future, covering the death of the sun, the end of stars, proton decay, black hole evaporation and the fate of the cosmos.
uD4izuDMUQA.why: HN people recommend it as a stunning, mind-bending and existentially humbling view of deep time, and it appears on lists of favorite YouTube videos.

uUmIdq0D6-A.summary: A long talk by rancher Gabe Brown on turning his North Dakota farm into a regenerative ecosystem using no-till, cover crops and integrated livestock. It covers the five principles of soil health and how they pay off financially.
uUmIdq0D6-A.why: HN commenters call it their favorite introduction to regenerative agriculture, and several say it changed how they garden or farm.

uxykI30fS54.summary: Not Just Bikes explains why the channel exists, through the creator's walk in suburban Houston. It shows how car-dependent design makes cities hostile to pedestrians.
uxykI30fS54.why: Strongly recommended as the entry point to a channel on urban planning and car dependency in North America.

u6XAPnuFjJc.summary: An RSA Animate whiteboard adaptation of Dan Pink's talk on what motivates people at work. It argues that beyond simple tasks, autonomy, mastery and purpose drive performance more than money.
u6XAPnuFjJc.why: HN uses it in discussions of pay, management, and motivation as the standard short explanation of autonomy, mastery and purpose.

uNjxe8ShM-8.summary: A short SIGBOVIK 2017 presentation by Tom Wildenhain showing that PowerPoint animations are Turing complete, with a working Turing machine built in slides. The talk is delivered deadpan as a serious research result.
uNjxe8ShM-8.why: HN repeatedly names it as one of the funniest and best talks, a favorite example of absurd computation.

u4ZoJKF_VuA.summary: Simon Sinek's TEDx talk arguing that great leaders and companies inspire action by communicating why they do something before how or what. He uses Apple as his main example.
u4ZoJKF_VuA.why: Recommended as a quick way to get the core of 'Start with Why' for pitches and communication, though some note small companies are not Apple.

u9KNtnCZDMI.summary: Media Molecule's Alex Evans recounts the journey, including the failures, of finding the Dreams engine, based on his Siggraph 2015 talk. It covers the signed-distance-field and splat-based rendering approach and the artistic goals behind it.
u9KNtnCZDMI.why: HN calls it an inspirational must-see on SDF rendering and a favorite tech talk for graphics programmers.

ue-1JoJQaEg.summary: Technology Connections takes a long, detailed look at how a 1970s electromechanical pinball machine works, from relays to stepper motors and mechanical logic. It is the first part of a series.
ue-1JoJQaEg.why: HN points people to it as a deep dive showing how complex logic was built without computers.

u404SLJj7ig.summary: Code Rush is a 2000 PBS documentary following Netscape engineers during the year they open-sourced the browser as Mozilla. It shows the pressure and long hours of work in Silicon Valley at the height of the dot-com era.
u404SLJj7ig.why: HN recommends it as a great tech documentary on Mozilla's open-sourcing and the hard work of Netscape engineers.

uL2D3qzHtqY.summary: Cliff Click of Azul Systems asks what a JVM is supposed to do, in a Google Tech Talk from 2011. He covers the services a JVM provides, such as garbage collection and compilation, and the messy reality beneath the abstractions.
uL2D3qzHtqY.why: A repeated recommendation for anyone interested in VMs, with Click's talks regarded as unusually informative on JVMs, JITs and the user/kernel boundary.

uOSnQM1Zu4w.summary: Practical Engineering explains what a black start is: restarting a power grid after total collapse. It shows why most plants need outside power to start and why rebuilding a synchronized grid is delicate and high-stakes.
uOSnQM1Zu4w.why: Go-to reference whenever a major blackout happens, recommended as an excellent explanation of why black starts are hard.

uk3A41U0iO4.summary: Matt Adereth's Clojure/conj talk covers the history of keyboards and how he used Clojure generating OpenSCAD to design and build his custom Dactyl ergonomic keyboard, including 3D printing and laser-cut parts.
uk3A41U0iO4.why: Recommended as a fantastic talk on code-driven CAD and custom keyboard design, linked in threads on OpenSCAD and keyboards.

uDr4L6BzpP8.summary: An Autoline After Hours episode where Sandy Munro discusses his complete teardown of the BMW i3, along with automotive journalists. It covers the car's carbon fiber construction and manufacturing technology.
uDr4L6BzpP8.why: HN recommends it as a fascinating look at the i3's revolutionary materials and production methods, and as a contrast point for Tesla.

uB0gr7Fh6lY.summary: Benn Jordan details security vulnerabilities in Flock Safety license-plate-reading cameras and how easily they can be compromised. It includes citations from security researchers and discussion of police surveillance.
uB0gr7Fh6lY.why: HN recommends it, and Jordan's wider Flock series, as a well-documented look at the poor security of these surveillance cameras.

uBh2LxTW0s0.summary: Andrew, diagnosed with early onset Parkinson's at 35, shows how deep brain stimulation surgery has controlled his motor symptoms. The short video shows his tremors with the stimulator off and on.
uBh2LxTW0s0.why: HN recommends it as a dramatic, moving demonstration of what deep brain stimulation can do for tremors.

uHQ4WCU1WQc.summary: An hour-long, carefully sourced video essay from Ahoy asking what counts as a video game and which one was truly first. It examines Tennis for Two, Spacewar, Pong, the Brown Box and a 1947 CRT device.
uHQ4WCU1WQc.why: HN recommends it as the thorough, well-researched answer to the first video game question.

uknEhXyZgsg.summary: A roughly two-hour demonstration by Dan Ingalls of Smalltalk running on the Computer History Museum's restored Xerox Alto. It shows the integrated environment and language designed at Xerox PARC as personal dynamic media.
uknEhXyZgsg.why: Recommended as a vivid look at live, interactive programming environments and what Xerox PARC built on very limited hardware.

uY-u1qyRM5w.summary: A 78-minute Richard Feynman lecture of anecdotes about working at Los Alamos on the Manhattan Project, followed by about ten minutes of audience Q&A in which he tells three safe-cracking stories.
uY-u1qyRM5w.why: Strongly recommended for its funny, human account of Los Alamos, which one commenter calls almost a stand-up act.

uYNzqgU7na4.summary: The Map Men explain why British place names are so hard to pronounce, tracing it to layers of Viking, Anglo-Saxon, Celtic and Norman influence, with a pronunciation guide.
uYNzqgU7na4.why: Recommended as an entertaining, short explanation whenever British place names or their linguistic history come up.

udPY5rQVoW0.summary: Sentdex demonstrates GAN Theft Auto, a GameGAN-based neural network that recreates GTA V so the network itself is the playable environment. He shows the results and releases the code.
udPY5rQVoW0.why: Cited as an early, striking demo of neural networks acting as game engines and world models.

uqKGREZs6-w.summary: A Kurzgesagt animation walking through how a Mars base could be built and why it would be punishing, covering radiation, temperature extremes, toxic dust and the need for shielding.
uqKGREZs6-w.why: Recommended as a sobering, accessible overview of the practical challenges of living on Mars.

u-x7PdnvCyI.summary: A 2007 Computer History Museum conversation in which Nvidia CEO Jen-Hsun Huang interviews TSMC founder Morris Chang. Chang recounts his career and the creation of the dedicated silicon foundry model.
u-x7PdnvCyI.why: Recommended as a rare, inspiring history of the foundry business and the relationship between Chang and Huang.

u5um8QWWRvo.summary: An RSA Animate drawing of Barbara Ehrenreich's talk on the darker side of positive thinking. It argues that forced positivity in culture, work and policy can be harmful and played a part in the financial crisis.
u5um8QWWRvo.why: HN uses it as a go-to short critique of mandatory positivity in workplaces, startups and corporate culture.

uTRUQ-RKfUs.summary: The first part of Lindsay Ellis's video essay series on the troubled production and critical reception of The Hobbit film trilogy.
uTRUQ-RKfUs.why: HN recommends it as an engaging analysis of how the Hobbit films were made, in threads on CGI and Tolkien.

uU_Q2a0S0zI.summary: Richard Hamming's 1995 lecture on n-dimensional space, showing how geometric intuition about spheres and cubes breaks down in high dimensions. It is part of his course on learning to learn.
uU_Q2a0S0zI.why: Recommended as the source for counterintuitive high-dimensional geometry and described as an eye opener.

uZgbKrDEzAs.summary: Jonathan Blow talks at Gamelab 2018 about the design decisions behind Jai, the programming language he is building for game programmers. He covers low-friction development, quality of life and the effects of compile times.
uZgbKrDEzAs.why: Recommended for a substantive look at language design priorities and a critique of why modern programming feels broken.

uaCaIhfETsM.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on the Sackler family and how they have handled opioid lawsuits. It covers how hard they fought to defend their name and is the third of three segments on the opioid crisis.
uaCaIhfETsM.why: Recommended in threads about Purdue and Sackler immunity as a good primer on the issue.

uqH_Y1TupoQ.summary: CGP Grey explains jury nullification, a juror's power to acquit despite the law, and why mentioning it can get you struck from jury selection.
uqH_Y1TupoQ.why: HN links it as the clearest short explainer of jury nullification and how the jury system works, often in threads on prosecutors and trials.

uxC1fPE1QEE.summary: Comedian Rob Paravonian's 'Pachelbel Rant', a comedy bit showing that the chord progression of Pachelbel's Canon underlies countless pop songs. This is a high-quality 2019 re-post of the 2006 original.
uxC1fPE1QEE.why: Recommended in threads on music copyright and chord progressions as a funny, accurate demonstration that a few chords are fundamental to music.

uDqjIdI4bF4.summary: Alan Becker's short series on the 12 principles of animation, covering squash and stretch, anticipation, staging, timing, arcs, appeal and the rest. Each principle gets a brief animated illustration.
uDqjIdI4bF4.why: Recommended as a compact starting point for making animations feel more compelling, including for UI and app developers.

uGlzRt-FYto.summary: Elm creator Evan Czaplicki's 2018 Elm Europe talk on how to define success for an open source project and language community. It argues against judging projects by GitHub activity and touches on community expectations.
uGlzRt-FYto.why: Cited in debates over Elm's direction and open source health, with some praising its points about metrics and others finding its tone toward unhappy users hard to watch.

uWUHkCgslNE.summary: A ShortCircuit (Linus Tech Tips) review of Nvidia's RTX Voice, which uses GPU-based neural networks to remove background noise from microphone audio. It demonstrates how well the filtering works.
uWUHkCgslNE.why: Cited as a demo of GPU-powered noise suppression that works remarkably well, in threads on mic muting and speech enhancement.

u_ktRTWMX3M.summary: A motivational compilation of Arnold Schwarzenegger's 2018 speech, delivered as inspiration about work and purpose.
u_ktRTWMX3M.why: HN users recommend it as practical motivation against procrastination and for people unsure what to do next.

umatbZ0n4mE.summary: Musician Thoj performs a live looping session on the Teenage Engineering OP-1 synthesizer, building a deep house track layer by layer.
umatbZ0n4mE.why: HN points to it as a demonstration of the OP-1, a well-designed instrument and an accessible way to start making music.

usSfgHGEGxQ.summary: Jacob Geller's video essay examines how architecture in schools and in video games, such as cover shooters, is shaped by violence. It touches on brutalism, campus policing and protests.
usSfgHGEGxQ.why: HN recommends it as an informed look at architecture in games and at how school design relates to shooter maps and Columbine.

uKfKtXYLG78.summary: A short film about the Erlang language, showing telecom systems built from lightweight processes and demonstrating hot code swapping. It is an edited version of the original Ericsson video.
uKfKtXYLG78.why: HN treats it as a classic that shows what Erlang was built for: robust, concurrent telecom systems with live upgrades.

uTdyb-RWNKo.summary: The official trailer for the documentary General Magic, about the secretive Apple spinoff that tried to build a handheld communicator in 1990 and whose ideas shaped the smartphone era.
uTdyb-RWNKo.why: HN recommends the documentary itself as a story of an epic early failure in mobile computing, and the trailer is the linked entry point.

uXdtafGdIVM.summary: Norm Macdonald's 2015 appearance on Letterman's final Late Show, delivering a deadpan bit about Germany and its military history. Jerry Seinfeld reportedly called it Norm's best joke.
uXdtafGdIVM.why: HN shares it as one of the greatest stand-up bits ever, and pulls it out whenever Germany, war or trade come up.

udJJ7n_Ryjg.summary: RethinkX summarizes its report arguing that mainstream LCOE estimates are inflating a bubble in coal, gas, nuclear and hydro assets. It claims solar, wind and batteries will strand conventional energy investments.
udJJ7n_Ryjg.why: Cited in nuclear-versus-renewables debates to support the argument that cheap renewables undercut new nuclear.

udlMSe5-zP8.summary: A long Joe Rogan podcast conversation with John Carmack covering his career, work habits, open source, AGI, quantum computing and CPUs.
udlMSe5-zP8.why: Recommended as a wide-ranging Carmack interview, noted for his views on work ethic and AGI.

u4L130DkdOw.summary: Anna Rosling Rönnlund presents Dollar Street, a project photographing homes in dozens of countries, from stoves to beds to toilets, and sorting them by income. She shows how data visualization can change how we see the world.
u4L130DkdOw.why: HN recommends it as an insightful, perspective-giving look at how people live across income levels, useful as a counter to pessimism.

u7TwqpWiY5s.summary: Conan O'Brien and Andy Richter visit Google's Mountain View headquarters in 2010 for a comedic Q&A. Conan jokes with the interviewer and the Google audience.
u7TwqpWiY5s.why: HN mentions it mainly for Conan's roasting of the interviewer and Google's leadership, not for any informational content.

uCsD3ZGzMgE.summary: Numberphile with Daniel Erman on the Josephus problem, where people in a circle are eliminated in turn. It shows how the survivor's position follows a neat pattern tied to powers of two and binary.
uCsD3ZGzMgE.why: HN cites it as an excellent example of solving small cases to find a pattern, and as a favorite puzzle with an elegant binary solution.

uF-GSj-Exms.summary: A 49-minute demo of Palantir Foundry by its chief architect. It walks through data integration, ML and AI workflows, analytics, and application building across the platform.
uF-GSj-Exms.why: Pointed to as the clearest explanation of what Foundry actually is, and for its polished software, though one commenter calls it dated now.

uFQ3sajIdaM.summary: CuriousMarc and colleagues at the Computer History Museum try to compile and run a FORTRAN II program on a 1959 IBM 1401. The machine has only 16k of memory and a CPU not meant for scientific work, so success is far from guaranteed.
uFQ3sajIdaM.why: Passed around in computing-history threads as a charming example of vintage hardware being coaxed into running FORTRAN.

uI1eRy0uBI8.summary: Big Clive does a complete teardown of a lithium phone battery, taking apart the protection circuit, case and the cell itself. He notes it was risky because the cell was not discharged first.
uI1eRy0uBI8.why: HN points to it in battery-fire threads as a rare look at what is inside a Li-ion cell and how dangerous disassembly really is.

uRe9w5PKmsE.summary: Big Clive takes apart an IKEA Koppla USB power supply to assess its safety, looking at isolation and transformer construction.
uRe9w5PKmsE.why: Cited as a teardown of a well-made, safe USB charger, and as evidence for why quality chargers matter.

uaje5I22kgE.summary: Anthony Scopatz presents xonsh at PyCon 2016, a shell that is a superset of Python combining the best features of bash, zsh and fish. It covers rich history, tab completion, and how the language compiles to a Python AST.
uaje5I22kgE.why: Recommended as the author's own explanation of xonsh's design and how Python and shell interplay.

uhbDfi7Ee7k.summary: Technology Connections looks at why awnings disappeared from houses and how effective they are at cutting solar heat gain and cooling costs. It argues they are a simple, forgotten cooling technology.
uhbDfi7Ee7k.why: HN brings it up in threads on cooling, window heat gain and house design as a convincing case for awnings.

ulCdoCfw-bY.summary: Kurzgesagt explains the black hole bomb and how far-future civilizations might extract energy from spinning black holes, including Dyson-sphere-style ideas.
ulCdoCfw-bY.why: Linked as a nice summary of how civilizations could harvest black hole energy.

upzKj-1HaKw.summary: A 1996 clip of Steve Jobs saying that Microsoft lacks taste and is not a creative company.
upzKj-1HaKw.why: Cited when HN discusses taste and vision in product companies.

uqY3FMuMuRo.summary: Ben Eater finishes building a minimal VGA video card from logic circuits. He explains analog RGB signals, stores an image in an EEPROM and builds a simple digital-to-analog converter to display it.
uqY3FMuMuRo.why: Recommended as an accessible, educational build that anyone with basic logic knowledge can follow.

uxPdPpi5W4o.summary: Veritasium rides a boat across the Los Angeles reservoir covered in 96 million black plastic balls. He explains why they were really introduced, which was not primarily to reduce evaporation.
uxPdPpi5W4o.why: Referenced as the explanation of shade balls and used in discussions of evaporation and floating covers.

uzkD5SeuwzM.summary: Kurzgesagt explains why, even with science-fiction technology, most of the universe is permanently out of reach because of cosmic expansion and finite resources.
uzkD5SeuwzM.why: Cited in cosmology threads as an accessible visual explanation of the unreachable universe and its expansion limits.

u69YSh-cFXY.summary: A student interviews Kirsten Carlson, who does not have an internal monologue, and she answers questions about how she thinks. The video grew out of a viral article about people lacking inner speech.
u69YSh-cFXY.why: HN refers to it as a vivid first-person account of anendophasia whenever inner monologues come up.

uA0Z7_4J7u8.summary: Edward Kmett's 2013 talk at Prezi in Budapest on succinct data structures, which store data in close to the information-theoretic minimum space while supporting fast queries. It ties together the research and walks through his Haskell succinct library.
uA0Z7_4J7u8.why: Commenters credit it as the place they first learned about succinct data structures, and found it left a lasting impression.

uBsJgceM0KI.summary: The first part of the ending alien sequence from the 2018 film Annihilation, with its distinctive soundtrack. The scene features a strange, shifting mimic and a surreal visual climax.
uBsJgceM0KI.why: It is recommended as a must-see scene in threads about unusual geometry and animation, such as Mandelbulb and 4D visuals.

uKxzK9xtSXM.summary: A clip in which Eben Moglen tells how he grew up when software was freer and how his path crossed Richard Stallman's. He describes how they came to work together to make software free again.
uKxzK9xtSXM.why: Cited for a short talk that frames graphical interfaces as point-and-grunt versus language-based Unix, and for showing Moglen's regard for Stallman.

uAdmzyKagvE.summary: Tom Scott explains the famous Dutch flower auction clock at Royal FloraHolland in Aalsmeer, a literal Dutch auction, and how the internet changed it. It is a short look at how the system worked then and now.
uAdmzyKagvE.why: HN cites it as a fascinating explanation of a real Dutch auction, in threads about auctions and ticket sales.

uCgnWqoP4MM.summary: Valve's short video on building the Steam Controller on a heavily automated assembly line, which the company designed itself. It shows the robotic manufacturing process and US final assembly.
uCgnWqoP4MM.why: HN cites it as a glimpse of in-house, highly automated hardware manufacturing and the scale of a lights-off factory.

uFvokQUHh08.summary: A Danish university math revue music video that parodies Barbra Streisand to explain the Banach-Tarski paradox, with oranges multiplying on stage.
uFvokQUHh08.why: HN people post it as a fun musical companion in threads on the Banach-Tarski theorem.

uNS6VKNXY6s.summary: Scott Manley uses a realistically scaled Kerbal Space Program setup to show why dropping something into the Sun is far harder than it sounds. It demonstrates the need to cancel orbital velocity.
uNS6VKNXY6s.why: Cited whenever someone suggests launching nuclear waste or other junk into the Sun, as a clear demonstration of the orbital mechanics involved.

uOJCS1W1uzg.summary: Quanta Magazine explains the 2022 experiment that claimed to create a holographic wormhole on Google's quantum computer. The description now notes that a later independent analysis questioned whether any wormhole was created.
uOJCS1W1uzg.why: Initially praised as a nicely done explainer, it is now more often cited as an example of overhyped quantum coverage.

uQHFQoFoxvQ.summary: A short experiment dissolving the aluminum of a Coca-Cola can with drain cleaner to reveal the clear plastic film lining inside.
uQHFQoFoxvQ.why: Cited as a vivid demonstration that beverage cans have a plastic liner.

uRGljemfwUE.summary: A comedy video in which a salesperson demands that a web developer fix a down website, with the two talking past each other. It won a Webby award.
uRGljemfwUE.why: HN treats it as a beloved piece of tech-workplace humor, quoted whenever an outage or sales-versus-engineering friction comes up.

uYbdx4I7STg.summary: Technology Connections explains how RGB light and color work, from hue and saturation to color vision and how objects appear under different lighting. It uses a studio setup with colored lights to demonstrate the effects.
uYbdx4I7STg.why: HN points to it as an accessible explanation of how color and reflected light behave, especially under LED lighting.

ua5aOFi-DKs.summary: Matt Parker of Stand-up Maths examines the Texas Supreme Court filing claiming Biden's 2020 win had a one-in-a-quadrillion chance. He walks through why the statistical argument is flawed.
ua5aOFi-DKs.why: Cited as a mathematician's debunking of numerical claims of 2020 election fraud.

ubDMLoWz76U.summary: Mitchell Hashimoto walks through his setup for running a NixOS virtual machine on a Mac as his development environment, with a config repo on GitHub.
ubDMLoWz76U.why: HN points to it as a practical reference for the Linux-VM-on-Mac workflow and as an entry point to NixOS.

ug-CyGXMabg.summary: A Ben Heck Show episode tearing down the Nintendo PlayStation prototype, one of the rarest consoles ever, with its owners Terry and Dan Diebold. Part 2 then gets it working again.
ug-CyGXMabg.why: HN uses it to show what the Nintendo PlayStation prototype hardware actually looked like, essentially an SNES with a CD-ROM drive.

uhwcEvMJz1Y.summary: A short clip from the British panel show QI in which the panel discusses why there is no such thing as a fish as a biological category.
uhwcEvMJz1Y.why: Linked in threads about fuzzy categories, such as fish, trees and fruit, as the origin of the phrase and a fun illustration.

unCQHAbGsAA.summary: The BotHack NetHack bot wins the game for the first time with no cheats or human intervention, in a run lasting about 3.5 hours. The description links the source code and the dumplog.
unCQHAbGsAA.why: Linked as the canonical video of the first fully automatic NetHack bot ascension in threads on NetHack and game-playing AI.

upsZZ2s3xv8.summary: An animated National Film Board of Canada short about a young woman who picks a log driver as her partner because his work makes him a great dancer. It is set to Wade Hemsworth's folk song sung by Kate and Anna McGarrigle.
upsZZ2s3xv8.why: It comes up as a beloved example of NFB animation and state-funded Canadian cultural work.

uwCwtBxZM7g.summary: A SIGGRAPH 2013 demo from Douglas Lanman and NVIDIA of near-eye light field displays, which allow much thinner head-mounted displays that still show accurate focus and depth cues.
uwCwtBxZM7g.why: HN cites it in Magic Leap and VR threads as a clear overview of how light fields could solve focus and bulk problems.

u-kkf76TDHE.summary: A GopherCon 2014 session where Blake Mizerany replaced his planned talk with a panel discussion with members of the Go team. It covers Go's design choices and community questions.
u-kkf76TDHE.why: HN commenters cite it as a source for what Go team members said about language regrets and Go's adoption.

u0hYIRQRiws.summary: A short side-by-side recording by Jake Archibald of the same animation demo running in Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Servo WebRender nightlies on a 60Hz display. It shows the smoothness difference of GPU-based rendering.
u0hYIRQRiws.why: Used as a quick visual benchmark of the performance gain WebRender brings in Firefox and Servo discussions.

u1Ds9CeG-VY.summary: The scene from the 2001 film Swordfish in which Hugh Jackman's character is forced to hack while under pressure. The clip is widely known for its absurd depiction of hacking.
u1Ds9CeG-VY.why: Used as a joke or shorthand for ridiculous movie hacking and unrealistic depictions of software work.

u2ZynkD3N_k.summary: A CNN news clip of President Obama drinking filtered Flint tap water during his visit to Flint, Michigan, over the lead contamination crisis.
u2ZynkD3N_k.why: Cited critically as an example of a political stunt meant to reassure the public about water safety.

u48vYSLvKNQ.summary: A short clip from HBO's Silicon Valley in which Gavin Belson fires the Nucleus team.
u48vYSLvKNQ.why: Posted as a joke in layoff threads, since the show already satirized exactly this kind of corporate layoff scenario.

u8qgehH3kEQ.summary: A one-minute NCIS scene in which two characters type on the same keyboard to fight off a hacker. It is widely mocked as absurd TV hacking.
u8qgehH3kEQ.why: Used as a joke or meme whenever threads mention fake TV hacking or pair programming.

uASUHbFEhWY.summary: A clip from Futurama's 'Attack of the Killer App' episode parodying the iPhone as the eyePhone.
uASUHbFEhWY.why: Posted as a joke in threads about AR headsets, wearables and Apple's future products.

uClWlVCwHsI.summary: Chuck Cook films Tesla FSD Beta 8.2 attempting unprotected left turns across forward-facing traffic, using a drone for a third-person view. Eight tests are shown with the car's on-screen visualizations.
uClWlVCwHsI.why: Used mostly as evidence of FSD Beta's limitations, for example pulling out in front of fast traffic.

uEY58fiSK8E.summary: A short clip of Louis C.K.'s Conan interview riff 'Everything's Amazing and Nobody's Happy', about how people take modern technology for granted and complain about marvels.
uEY58fiSK8E.why: HN uses it as a reference when commenters want to point out how quickly people forget the wonder of modern technology and complain anyway.

uEx5G-GOS1k.summary: A one-minute Eddie Izzard comedy clip about how the British Empire claimed countries by planting flags. It riffs on the absurd rule of 'no flag, no country'.
uEx5G-GOS1k.why: Mostly posted as a joke in threads about flags, empires and colonial trading companies.

uFpK_r-jEXg.summary: A 2009 satirical news segment from The Onion's 'In The Know' in which pundits adjust their on-air opinions in real time according to a live viewer poll. It lampoons pandering media and politics.
uFpK_r-jEXg.why: Used as a punchline whenever commenters see consensus-driven decisions, politicians chasing public opinion, or metric-driven content.

uLlv_aZjHXc.summary: The classic Monty Python sketch in which a man visits an Argument Clinic to buy an argument. It is a wordplay-heavy bit about contradiction versus real argument.
uLlv_aZjHXc.why: Invoked as a joke whenever online discussions devolve into pointless contradiction or arguing for its own sake.

uMM0lRfX6YI.summary: A one-minute Tesla clip showing a prototype robotic snake charger that finds a Model S's charge port and plugs itself in.
uMM0lRfX6YI.why: Brought up whenever robotic or automatic EV charging comes up, as the memorable 2015 demo that never became a product.

uMgTIlgYB-U.summary: The ElixirConf 2019 day 1 morning keynote, including the announcement of Lumen, an alternative BEAM implementation designed for WebAssembly. It features DockYard's team presenting the project and a demo.
uMgTIlgYB-U.why: HN links it as the original announcement of Lumen (later Firefly), for people wanting technical detail on the project.

uSVqoW1rz6w.summary: A fireside chat at TNW Conference where Reddit CEO Steve Huffman discusses Reddit's growth, user engagement and monetisation plans.
uSVqoW1rz6w.why: HN uses it mostly critically, as evidence of Huffman's attitude toward user data and community trust.

uTDO-kuOGTQ.summary: A short clip of Robert Mueller speaking about Iraq and weapons of mass destruction.
uTDO-kuOGTQ.why: Cited by critics to argue Mueller helped justify the Iraq war.

uUAvXYW5bmI.summary: A NASA video on the 29 days after the James Webb Space Telescope's launch, when thousands of parts must deploy in sequence on the way to its destination a million miles away.
uUAvXYW5bmI.why: Cited as an overview of JWST's complex deployment and its many single points of failure.

uVdDXeYM4ss.summary: A one-minute Steve Summers clip of Willy Wonka saying no, don't, stop. It is a reaction meme.
uVdDXeYM4ss.why: HN uses it only as a joke when someone is about to do something ill-advised, such as microservices.

uXlQuTRSmzc.summary: Tom Scott shows a robot double of himself, built from an Engineered Arts Mesmer robot, delivering a VPN advertisement in his place.
uXlQuTRSmzc.why: Linked as an example of the honest, self-aware way Tom Scott treats VPN ads and their legitimate use cases.

uc6QxD2_yQw.summary: A Pop Culture Detective video essay on how jokes about men sexually assaulting other men are common in entertainment media. Part 1 focuses on male perpetrators.
uc6QxD2_yQw.why: Cited as a resource on male victims of sexual assault and on prison rape jokes in media.

ucEs0nBuowE.summary: A BBC News clip of Putin pressing Russian foreign intelligence chief Sergei Naryshkin to speak clearly during a televised meeting on recognizing the rebel-held Ukrainian regions in February 2022.
ucEs0nBuowE.why: HN cites it as a glimpse of a fearful, disorganized Russian leadership just before the invasion of Ukraine.

ue7wM0QC5LE.summary: The classic Monty Python sketch in which four Yorkshiremen compete to claim the hardest upbringing, each story more absurd than the last.
ue7wM0QC5LE.why: Quoted as a joke whenever commenters one-up each other on past hardships.

ugvHCXCOmm4.summary: A roughly five-hour Lex Fridman podcast episode with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, plus Amanda Askell on Claude's character and Chris Olah on mechanistic interpretability. It covers Claude, AGI and the future of AI.
ugvHCXCOmm4.why: Mostly cited as a source for statements by Anthropic leaders, such as views on AI progress and on sycophancy.

uiCeqySVhCE.summary: A Foreign Correspondents' Club Hong Kong conversation with Noam Chomsky on COVID-19, Donald Trump, the New Cold War and the Hong Kong protests.
uiCeqySVhCE.why: Used as a source for Chomsky's quotes on neoliberalism, polarization, and trust crises during the pandemic.

uiDMlFycNrw.summary: A clip from the movie Minority Report showing personalized advertising that recognizes a person as they walk through a mall.
uiDMlFycNrw.why: Cited as the sci-fi precedent whenever HN discusses facial recognition and personalized ads in public spaces.

uiJycy6dFSQ.summary: Paul Phillips, a Typesafe co-founder and prolific Scala committer, explains why he walked away from Scala. He critiques the Scala collections library and presents his own design focused on immutability, performance and correctness.
uiJycy6dFSQ.why: Cited in Scala-skeptic arguments as an insider's critique, and for his alternative collections API design.

uj0mtxXEGE8.summary: A Chris Rock sketch giving comedic advice on how to behave during police encounters to avoid getting hurt.
uj0mtxXEGE8.why: HN cites it as a darkly funny, often-quoted take on police encounters, referenced in policing and parenting threads.

ukgnU2aXM2c.summary: A TEDxNashville talk by uBeam founder Meredith Perry about becoming a technology innovator and her plan for wireless charging of phones.

umJsITGzXd0.summary: Apple's 1987 Knowledge Navigator concept video, made for John Sculley's EDUCOM keynote, showing a professor conversing with a tablet-based AI assistant.
umJsITGzXd0.why: HN uses it as the classic early vision of conversational AI assistants, compared against modern AI products.

uo9nGzIzSPw.summary: A one-minute clip where an AM radio station can be heard through the arcing of a high-power transmitter tower.
uo9nGzIzSPw.why: Shared as a curiosity showing that with enough power almost anything can demodulate AM radio.

up863eQKGUI.summary: The 1992 SIIA anti-piracy rap video Don't Copy That Floppy, warning kids against copying software, remastered and uploaded.
up863eQKGUI.why: Referenced only as a nostalgic, cringeworthy joke in threads about floppies and piracy.

urcL86UpqZc.summary: Kai Lentit's comedy sketch parodies a retro documentary interview with an Emacs enthusiast, joking about Emacs's endless configuration and devotion.
urcL86UpqZc.why: Shared as a joke whenever Emacs obsession and configuration come up.

utfbE3_uAMA.summary: Strange Parts spends four months, seven custom circuit boards and several disassembled iPhones adding a working headphone jack to an iPhone 7 in China. The build is documented in detail.
utfbE3_uAMA.why: Cited as proof that space existed for a headphone jack in the iPhone.

uvPbj9NX0zc.summary: The Life of Brian scene in which revolutionaries list what the Romans have done for them, from aqueducts to roads, despite their complaints.
uvPbj9NX0zc.why: Used as a joke whenever a discussion has someone grudgingly listing the benefits of something they criticize.

uw8MACDZ3RI.summary: A short documentary by Christopher Rufo presenting a conservative account of homelessness, addiction and public disorder in San Francisco.
uw8MACDZ3RI.why: HN uses it as one of many clips documenting San Francisco's decline, and some commenters criticize it as pushing a point of view.

uwajp0g-bY4.summary: A short excerpt of Rob Pike's Lang.NEXT 2014 talk where he describes Go's target audience as young Google programmers who are not researchers. The language has to be easy for them to understand and adopt.
uwajp0g-bY4.why: Cited to show who Go was designed for, often in critiques of the language's simplicity.

uycsfu4574w.summary: A Monty Python sketch in which Oscar Wilde, James Whistler and George Bernard Shaw trade witticisms in a stuffy literary salon with Bertie.
uycsfu4574w.why: Used as a joke when commenters mention Oscar Wilde or the tone of literary salons.

uzV_uzSTCTM.summary: Dave Jones of EEVblog debunks the marketing claims of the self-charging nano nuclear diamond battery from NDB Inc. He argues it is no better than existing 100uW betavoltaic batteries, with an added graphene supercapacitor.
